modelName: Cartographic Relief Shading with Neural Networks
aiTask: Image-to-image translation (DEM to shaded relief rendering)
inputSpecification:
- Raster digital elevation model (DEM)
- Format: raster grid (e.g. GeoTIFF or equivalent)
- Input values: elevation normalised to [0,1]
- Tile-based processing (typically 256x256 or 512x512 pixels)
- No additional terrain derivatives required (e.g. slope, aspect)
- Consistent resolution with training data recommended
outputSpecification:
- Grayscale raster image (shaded relief)
- Same spatial reference as input DEM
- Continuous intensity values representing illumination and terrain structure
- No explicit class schema
- No confidence scores provided
architecture: Modified U-Net convolutional neural network (encoder-decoder with skip connections)
trainingDataOrigin: - Manual shaded relief maps from Swiss national map series (swisstopo) - Paired with corresponding digital elevation models - Geographic scope: Switzerland - Multi-scale cartographic products (1:50,000 and smaller scales) - Contains subjective cartographic generalisation and stylistic decisions
primaryPerformanceMetric: Expert evaluation: majority rating good to very good by 18 cartographic experts

modelName: Large Rock Detection from Aerial Imagery
inputSpecification:
- High-resolution aerial imagery (swissIMAGE, RGB)
- Digital elevation model (swissALTI3D)
- Derived hillshade from DEM
- Raster tiles (processed in tiles, typically aligned to Swiss grid)
- Input size: 640 × 640 pixels
- Geographic constraint: Switzerland (trained on Alpine terrain)
- Requires preprocessing including DEM-derived features and tiling
outputSpecification:
- Bounding boxes representing detected rocks
- Output stored in DuckDB and exported to GeoPackage (.gpkg)
- Spatially referenced detections aligned with input tiles
- Confidence score per detection
- Object definition: large rocks ≥ approx. 5×5×5 m
trainingDataOrigin: - ~4,000 manually annotated rock instances from swisstopo - Additional ~900 negative samples (urban areas, glaciers) - Geographic scope: Switzerland (mainly Alpine regions) - Input sources: swissIMAGE (RGB) and swissALTI3D (DEM) - Annotation format: point annotations converted to bounding boxes (~15 m size)
primaryPerformanceMetric: Recall ≈ 74% and Precision ≈ 63% on independent test set (327 annotated rocks)
moreInformation: The model detects large rock formations using combined RGB imagery and elevation-derived features. It is optimized for Alpine terrain and favors recall over precision, requiring manual filtering of false positives. The pipeline includes automatic data download, tiling, inference, and geospatial output generation. Confidence thresholds can be adjusted to trade off completeness vs. accuracy.

modelName: MinkUNet14A for Tower--Conductor Segmentation in ALS LiDAR Point Clouds
inputSpecification: The model expects a voxel grid as an input. The model was trained on LiDAR point clouds with XYZ coordinates expressed in meters. Raw LiDAR Point clouds must be voxelized at a resolution of 10 cm (0.10 m). Only XYZ coordinate information is used as input, no additional voxel-level attributes.
outputSpecification: For the full voxel grid, the model outputs a binary segmentation mask with the interpretation of 0 -> "Conductor" and 1 -> "Tower". Voxel predictions are mapped back to point coordinates for the final output.
trainingDataOrigin: Annotated private and publicly available datasets (see more information)
moreInformation:
The model was developed to semantically refine transmission corridor ALS point clouds into the classes tower and conductor. The model has been validated across 5 different datasets (private: DigiZ-DE [1], publicly available: DALES [2], ECLAIR [3], GridNetHD [4], TowerDataset [5]) with performance varying between 91 - 98 mIoU.

----------------
[1] Digitaler Zwilling Deutschland (DigiZ-DE): https://www.bkg.bund.de/DE/Forschung/Projekte/Digitaler-Zwilling/Digitaler-Zwilling_cont.html
[2] Varney et al. 2020, DALES: A large-scale aerial LiDAR data set for semantic segmentation.
[3] Melekhov et al. 2024,  Eclair: A high-fidelity aerial lidar dataset for semantic segmentation
[4] Carreaud et al. 2026, GridNet-HD: A High-Resolution Multi-Modal Dataset for LiDAR-Image Fusion on Power Line Infrastructure
[5] Cui et al., 2026, TowerDataset: A Heterogeneous Benchmark for Transmission Corridor Segmentation with a Global-Local Fusion Framework

modelName: Object Classification for Aviation Obstacle Identification in ALS LiDAR Point Clouds
inputSpecification: The input data is binary numpy arrays derived from LAS 1.4 ALS point clouds. Single Photon Lidar (SPL) has been used for the survey. The following features were used: XYZ + Intensity, Height Above Ground, NumberOfReturns, ReturnNumber
outputSpecification: The model outputs object-wise single class label. The class schema consists of 9 different classes: Power poles, power lines, towers, wind mills, 3 different crane types, noise and other
trainingDataOrigin: 1,000 self-annotated objects > 40 m height above ground from the pilot project of the Digital Twin Germany. The region covers the metropolitan region of Hamburg (~8600 km²). The survey was conducted with an SPL sensor in winter 2021/2022.
moreInformation:
Within the Digital Twin Germany (DigiZ-DE) [1] aviation obstacles are being identified from 3D ALS data. The obstacle type is usually derived from the dominant semantic class already present in the data, but more detailed information about the obstacles is needed. In a preprocessing pipeline high objects > 40 m from the "Unclassified" class are extracted using rule-based methods and clustered and afterwards fed into a PointNet, trained from scratch, for object-wise classification. The training data is imbalanced, resulting in varying class-wise performance. For major classes such as wind turbines, power poles, and power lines, the model achieves approximately 95% precision, recall, and F1-score.

[1] Digitaler Zwilling Deutschland (DigiZ-DE): https://www.bkg.bund.de/DE/Forschung/Projekte/Digitaler-Zwilling/Digitaler-Zwilling_cont.html

modelName: SAMLoRA for Building Construction Site Detection
inputSpecification: The input data are True Orthophotos (RGB) with 20 cm spatial resolution  in the form of image chips with size 1024x1024 px.
outputSpecification: The model outputs a raster image of confidence values between 0 and 1 (construction/no construction). From that values over 0.5 are converted to a binary mask and lastly vectorized to polygons. The geospatial properties of the input data are preserved.
architecture: ViT Backbone Segment Anything Model + Low Rank Adaption Layers
trainingDataOrigin: Labels of construction sites were created manually from selected ortophotos.
moreInformation:
The model is developed in the context of a joint project between BKG and the German Federal Statistical Office called "EO4ConStat". The goal is the creation of a dataset that can be used in the quality assurance of the German construction statistics. 
The same model architecture was also successfully tested on meadow orchards, using a curated training dataset from OSM data and manually corrected/created orchard labels. Both models were prototyped in the German county North-Rhine-Westphalia.

modelName: Solar panels detection with post-processing focused on ground-mounted panels

outputSpecification: 1 band raster with 2 classes: solar panel and other. \nAfter post-processing output is: geopackage with polygons of ground-mounted solar parks. Number of panels in solar park is included as attribute.
moreInformation: In combination with existing Estonian Topographic Database and post-processing the precision of new solar parks detected is ~80-90% (from 600 \"potential solar park\" polygons ~500-570 will be real ones)
